## 2. The residence operation is completely constructed in a rough-interface sector

The ordered-current theorem is useful beyond a formal reduction: there is a nontrivial sector in which its current can be written and evaluated explicitly.

Let
\[
\eta\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{m},\qquad
\eta_0=\eta_{m+1}=0,
\]
with energy
\[
E(\eta)
=
2J\sum_{j=0}^{m}|\eta_{j+1}-\eta_j|
-2h\sum_{j=1}^{m}\eta_j.
\]
Use the actual heat-bath rates for the allowed single-height changes, reflecting moves outside this graph-interface sector. Every permitted change corresponds to one physical spin clock.

Reflect the lower wall and kill at
\[
B_\uparrow=\{\max_j\eta_j=H\}.
\]
Assume \(m\ge2R\).

Whole-interface translation has energy increment
\[
d=E(\eta+\mathbf1)-E(\eta)=4J-2hm\le0.
\]
Realize it by the prefix path
\[
\eta^{(k)}=\eta+\mathbf1_{\{j\le k\}},
\qquad k=0,\ldots,m.
\]
For every rough profile,
\[
E(\eta^{(k)})-E(\eta)\le4J.
\]

The crucial entropy accounting is exact: an upward edge at coordinate \(k\), starting from \(z\), uniquely determines the translation source,
\[
\eta_j=z_j-\mathbf1_{\{j<k\}}.
\]
The construction retains the rough profile instead of merging many profiles into a flat one.

Along each translation orbit, define
\[
F_{\rm tr}(\eta,\eta+\mathbf1)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\eta}w(\eta-\ell\mathbf1)
=
w(\eta)\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\eta}e^{\beta d\ell}
\le H w(\eta).
\]
This flow has divergence exactly \(w(\eta)\). Serialize it along the prefix paths and stop upon reaching the upper wall. Unique decoding and the heat-bath conductance identity give
\[
0\le\frac{F(e)}{g(e)}\le2He^{4\theta}.
\]
An increasing height path has at most \(mH\) edges. The current-path theorem, together with attractiveness of the height dynamics, therefore proves
\[
\boxed{
\sup_\eta\mathbb E_\eta\tau_{B_\uparrow}
\le2mH^2e^{4\theta},
\qquad m\ge2R.
}
\tag{4}
\]

Each flow value is computed by decoding one translation source and evaluating one geometric sum. There is no partition-function acquisition, minimum-state-mass logarithm, or enumeration of all profiles in this construction.

For the separate decision problem killed when either \(\min\eta=0\) or \(\max\eta=H\), the same prefix comparison gives
\[
\boxed{
\lambda_{\rm kill}\ge\frac{e^{-4\theta}}{mH^2}.
}
\tag{5}
\]
